messages:
elena: Heads-up — customer CS-4821 sees tool outputs getting swapped when they invoke multiple tools in parallel. The payload returns tool_result for the wrong tool (confidentiality risk). Repro steps below.
frank: yikes. any request ids or logs we can look at?
elena: gave them req id `req_0a7c2b9f` and two correlation ids `corr-6112` / `corr-6113`. Logs show both tool pipelines executed on same host but final response maps tool_result IDs incorrectly.
sam: can you paste the minimal request they used? are they using function-calling or our legacy tool endpoint?
elena: function-calling wrapper. here's a redacted minimal payload they used (they said parallel=true):
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-redwood-2",
  "input": "Check price and inventory for SKU X1",
  "tools": [
    {"name": "price_lookup", "args": {"sku": "X1"}},
    {"name": "inventory_check", "args": {"sku": "X1"}}
  ],
  "tool_options": {"invoke_mode": "parallel"}
}
```
elena: curl they used: `curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/function_call -d @payload.json`
tariq: I took a quick look at the runtime code path. There's a race in the tool_result association map: we keyed by `parent_request_ts` instead of a per-tool invocation uuid when tools are spawned concurrently. If two tool calls finish close enough, one write can overwrite the other's entry. That matches the symptom.
maria: which runtime version was this on? can we get worker logs around `req_0a7c2b9f`?
elena: customer on runtime `v2.14.1`. Redacted worker log snippet they provided:
```
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f tool=price_lookup invoc=0x9f2 start
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f tool=inventory_check invoc=0x9f3 start
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f tool=inventory_check invoc=0x9f3 result=result_88a
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f tool=price_lookup invoc=0x9f2 result=result_88b
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f assoc_map_write key=1678458724 value=result_88a
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f assoc_map_write key=1678458724 value=result_88b
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z worker=infra-5 request=req_0a7c2b9f final_response tool_results=[result_88b, result_88b]
```
elena: note the assoc_map_write uses epoch key `1678458724` — that's the root of the bug.
frank: quick patch idea: switch assoc key to `request_id + invocation_uuid` and guard writes with a mutex or atomic map ops. I can prototype a fix + unit test.
sam: can we get a small repro test in our infra so we don't have to repro on customer's data? I can run a harness that spawns N parallel tool calls under same parent request.
maria: also need to know if any customers saw PII leak; if tool results are swapped between different parent requests that’s higher severity. For CS-4821 looks like only within same parent request but still bad.
support-bot: Ticket CS-4821 updated and assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: P1 (customer-facing). https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-4821 :white_check_mark:
elena: temporary mitigation suggested to customer: set `tool_options.invoke_mode = "sequential"` or serialize calls client-side until we ship fix. They confirmed workaround works.
tariq: I'll own the codefix. Plan: add per-invocation UUID, replace epoch key, add unit+concurrency tests, and deploy in canary. Expect patch PR today, canary tomorrow.
maria: please post PR link and ETA for rollback/patch notes so CS can update KB.
frank: PR will include test that spawns 100 parallel tool invocations and asserts unique mapping. quick + dirty patch in branch `fix/tool-assoc-uuid-2112`.
sam: I'll run the repro locally against canary when ready. :thumbsup:
elena: thanks — keeping CS and customer in loop. I'll paste any further logs here.
